curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8416-1-1.pdf (the forklift, functions on page 103; book 2, omr/instructions/8416-1-2.pdf, builds the alternate tractor)

functions.does: The crank at the back raises and lowers the forks: through a 20- and a 12-tooth double bevel gear and a pair of 16-tooth gears it turns a long shaft forward under the cab, then bevel gears and two universal joints carry the drive up the mast to a worm, which turns a 24-tooth crown gear on a cross axle whose two 16-tooth gears climb the racks on the inner mast. The inner mast rises, and strings over the pulleys at its top lift the fork carriage up it at the same time.
functions.source: book 1: page 103 (arrows on the crank at the back); steps 6-8 on pages 83-84 (worm, crown gear and universal joint), 7-10 on pages 65-68 (racks on the inner mast), 10-12 on pages 73-77 (strings and pulleys; the page 77 inset shows the inner mast and forks rising), 19 on page 15 (crank and 20-tooth double bevel gear)
functions.note: That the carriage rises on its strings as the inner mast rises (a two-stage mast) is read from the page 77 inset and the strings' ends (p189 and p207 on the carriage, p304 and p305 on the outer mast). The worm holds the forks wherever they're left.

functions.does: The levers at the front edge of the cab roof tilt the mast: they turn a crank on the roof, whose two red suspension arms push and pull the top of the mast, and the mast pivots on two pins at the front axle.
functions.source: book 1: page 103 (curved arrows on the roof levers); steps 42-45 (roof), the red arms on pages 88-96, and step 18 on page 99 (mast mounted on the chassis)
functions.note: Which parts a person pushes is read from the arrows on page 103 (the roof's front liftarms p25, p34, p38, p45 on the crank's axles); the book doesn't say how far the mast tilts.

functions.does: The beacon on the cab roof is a knob that steers the rear wheels: its axle runs down through the cab to a pair of bevel gears, and two 8-tooth gears slide a rack sideways between the rear steering knuckles.
functions.source: book 1: steps 14-19 on pages 10-15 (rear steering rack, 8-tooth gears and knuckles), 48 on pages 52-53 (beacon on its axle); inferred: that the beacon is the steering knob, from the gears in the model file (page 103 draws no arrow on it)

functions.does: The four wheels roll freely; nothing drives them.
The steering wheel in the cab is for show: it sits on an axle pin and turns, but isn't linked to the wheels.
functions.source: book 1: step 44 (steering wheel on its pin); inferred: nothing connects it to the steering

functions.does: The pallet is loose: it rests on the forks and is carried by them.
functions.source: book 1: step 19 (pallet, pages 100-101) and step 20 (pallet on the forks)
functions.note: an accessory, not worked; it should rise and tilt with the forks

questions.question: Is the beacon the steering, the mast two-stage, the tilt worked by the roof levers?
